task: Review this undergraduate logic exercise and return the explanation unchanged if it is correct. Readers understand the fictional token rule but are practicing necessary and sufficient. The example explains those terms through the given relationship, so a short answer is appropriate. Do not impose a research-question opening, counterargument, or claim about a gate absent from the rule. This is a classroom model, not instructions for a real access system.
input: In this exercise, every copper token opens the inner gate, but some wooden tokens open it too. Being copper is therefore sufficient, not necessary, for opening that gate. The rule says nothing about the outer gate, so no conclusion about that gate follows.

facts.text: In the fictional rule system, every copper token opens the inner gate.
Some wooden tokens also open the inner gate.
No rule about the outer gate is supplied.
For this system, being copper is sufficient but not necessary for opening the inner gate.

forbidden_additions: A claim that only copper tokens open the inner gate
An invented rule that opens or closes the outer gate
A claim of uncertainty about the settled implication within the supplied model
preserve: Some wooden tokens are counterexamples to necessity
The inner-gate rule does not determine the outer gate
